essence: A city of water whose overlapping networks of canals and streets, laid on many levels, let every inhabitant reach the same places by a new route each day, while secret lives travel over the roofs and under the ground and the swallows' paths escape every map.
textDetails: Esmeralda is a city of water in which a network of canals and a network of streets overlap and cross each other.
To go anywhere one can always choose between land and boat.
The shortest way between two points is not a straight line but a zigzag that branches into many winding alternatives, multiplied further for those who alternate boat and foot.
So its people are spared the tedium of walking the same streets every day.
The routes do not lie on one level: they rise and fall by steps, landings, humpbacked (cambered) bridges and hanging streets.
By combining raised and ground-level stretches, each inhabitant can take a new itinerary to the same places every day; even the most settled lives never repeat.
Secret and adventurous lives are more constrained: cats, thieves and illicit lovers travel higher, broken routes, dropping from roof to balcony and following gutters with an acrobat's step.
Below, rats scurry through the dark sewers, each behind the other's tail, together with conspirators and smugglers.
They peer out of manholes and drainpipes, slip through false bottoms and ditches, and haul crusts of cheese, contraband and kegs of gunpowder from one hiding place to the next.
The compact body of the city is pierced by the spokes of underground passages.
A map of Esmeralda would have to mark all these routes, solid and liquid, evident and hidden, in inks of different colours.

Hardest to map are the swallows, cutting the air above the roofs in long invisible parabolas on still wings, darting to catch a mosquito, spiralling upward, grazing a pinnacle, commanding every point of the city from their flight.
Not in the text: specific buildings (the bell tower here is a staging anchor for the pinnacle the swallows graze), house colours, or the plan of the canals; the Italian name is Smeraldina.
visualConcept: A dense island city floating on an emerald lagoon, built as a deep cut-away block: above the water a maze of ochre, rose and sienna houses with terracotta roofs, crossed by canals and alleys; below the waterline, revealed in section on the side facing the viewer, a dark underworld of sewers and tunnels radiating like spokes from a central cistern. Every level is stitched to the others by humpbacked bridges, flights of steps, landings, balconies and hanging streets that leap between upper floors, so each place connects to every other by many paths. Three worlds move at once: boats and walkers on the solid and liquid routes; cats, thieves and illicit lovers making broken leaps across roofs and along gutters; rats running nose to tail through the sewers with smugglers rolling powder kegs, popping out of manholes and drainpipes. Above everything a flock of swallows drops long parabolas on still wings, darts after mosquitoes, spirals upward and grazes the pinnacle of a tall bell tower. Every moving thing leaves a short trail in its own ink (sepia for walkers, ultramarine for boats, crimson for roof-runners, violet-black for the underground, faint gold for swallows), so the city's many routes show as a living, multicoloured map. A single citizen with a small lantern travels each cycle from her door to the bell-tower square by a different route, mixing quay, bridge, steps, hanging street and boat, embodying the promise that no one need repeat a path. Trails are ring-buffered line strips with per-vertex alpha fading by age.
layout: North = -z. Lagoon disc radius 24, water plane at y=0 (emerald, reflective, small waves). City block radius 15 with street level at y=0.35 and a foundation slab down to y=-4; a 100-degree sector facing south (+z, toward the default camera) is cut away in section, showing strata of brick and silt, timber piles and the underworld: 8 tunnel spokes (tubes radius 0.35 at y=-1.5 to -2.5) radiating from a central cistern (radius 1.4) to a ring sewer at radius 11, with vertical shafts up to about 12 manholes in the streets. Canals: a grand canal 2.4 wide on an S-curve from west to east plus 9 minor canals 1.0 to 1.4 wide, cutting the block into about 14 islets, with quays along most banks. About 110 buildings (footprints 1 to 2.2, 3 to 5 storeys of 0.42, pitched terracotta roofs, chimneys, balconies on 40%), about 20 humpbacked bridges (span 1.2 to 2.6, rise 0.45), 6 hanging streets (walkways at y=1.3 to 1.9 bridging canals and lanes between upper floors), 12 flights of steps with landings. Central square 4 x 3 at about (1, 0.35, -1) with the bell tower: 1.2 x 1.2 shaft to y=6.5, open belfry, pyramidal pinnacle to y=8.6. Agents: 12 boats, about 60 walkers, 8 cats, 4 thieves and 2 pairs of lovers on the roofs, about 80 rats in chains of 10, 6 smugglers with kegs below, 30 swallows between y=3 and y=14, mosquito specks over the canals.
signatureMotion: 1) A new route every day: one citizen with a small lantern leaves her house on the west side and reaches the bell-tower square by a route freshly chosen from the path graph every 25 s cycle (for example quay, bridge, boat, steps, hanging street), drawn as a golden trail; earlier days' trails linger faintly, so many routes to one place accumulate. 2) Three-level traffic with ink trails: boats glide and turn at canal junctions, walkers rise and dip over humpbacked bridges, cats and thieves hop from roof to balcony in quick parabolic leaps and run along gutters, while rats stream nose to tail through the tunnel spokes, heads popping out of manholes, and smugglers roll their kegs. 3) Swallows: 30 birds on long ballistic arcs with motionless swept wings, sudden darts (a mosquito speck vanishes), tight upward spirals and close passes across the pinnacle; their faint gold trails fade within a second.
interactionDescription: Turns the city into its own map: colours drain to warm paper tones, the camera rises toward plan view, and from then on every route is laid down permanently in its ink (sepia streets, ultramarine canals, crimson roof leaps, violet-black sewers), accumulating into a dense, multicoloured chart of solid and liquid, evident and hidden ways. Only the swallows refuse to be fixed: their gold strokes keep fading as soon as they are drawn. Toggling back restores colour and lets the inks fade.
mood: Early summer, late afternoon: low golden sun raking across water and plaster, deep emerald canals with dancing reflections, a light green-gold haze over the lagoon, cool shade in the lanes and darkness in the tunnels lit only by a few lanterns; busy, intricate and warm, with swallows high and loud.
caption: Esmeralda is drawn twice over the same ground, once in streets and once in canals, and the two drawings braid together on bridges, stairs and hanging lanes. No one need take the same way twice: quay, then boat, then steps, then boat again. Above, cats and secret lovers leap from roof to balcony; below, rats and smugglers file through the sewers with cheese and powder kegs. Only the swallows' paths, flung across the sky, escape every map.
motto: Every day the same door, never the same way there.
camera: Three-quarter view from the south, distance about 40 units, elevation about 32 degrees, target the bell tower's base (about (1, 1.5, -1)): the cut-away section with its tunnels faces the viewer in the lower third, canals and roofs fill the middle, swallows wheel against the sky in the upper third; in map mode the camera rises to about 70 degrees.
